synopsis: The booklet treats Waymo and Motional as on-road vendor precedents for layered validation: simulation, replay and shadow mode filter candidates before scarce physical testing, rather than replace it [f15718, f15729]. Waymo published its collision avoidance testing methodology in 2022 and documented city-by-city expansion as evidence accumulates; the booklet cites these programs as evidence for staged release within a limited operating domain [f604, f15720, f15730]. Motional’s 2026 material describes progression from simulation and recorded-data re-simulation through closed-course and public-road testing to deployment, including daily shadow-mode evaluation before broader roll-out [f15725, f15726]. The booklet recommends shadow mode on the existing warning-only fleet as the most valuable lever for collecting false-positive evidence before the prototype arrives; Motional’s example runs new software without executing its actuator decisions [f15731, f15727]. Waymo’s material also distinguishes replay from closed-loop simulation and highlights reproducible dataset requirements and inconsistent human labeling, but neither developer discloses validation durations or physical-test shares sufficient for verified sign-off, and Waymo’s 2026 scene-generation world model has no off-road qualification [f15721, f15722, f15723, f15728, f15724].
